chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur and 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If you come to the well while you are in janabah and do not find a bucket or anything with which to draw water, then perform tayammum with the earth, for indeed the Lord of water is the Lord of the earth. And do not fall into the well, and do not spoil the people's water for them.

key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: the earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.دَلْوًا: a bucket used to draw water from a well
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum as the prescribed alternative purification
key_terms.مَاءَهُمْ: their water, meaning the water belonging to the people or community

ai.seo_question: What should a person in janabah do if water is present in a well but cannot be drawn?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one in janabah who reaches a well but cannot access its water. It instructs him to perform tayammum instead, while also forbidding him from contaminating or damaging the community's water source, combining ritual purity with the protection of others' rights.
